subject: Business Models
title: The Support Burden
description: A 60-second lesson on The Support Burden.

hook.text: Free users file support tickets too. They cost money to help but generate zero revenue in return.

buildup.text: Customer support is one of the largest costs in SaaS. Each ticket costs $5-$50 depending on complexity.

discovery.text: Smart companies restrict support for free tiers: community forums only, no live chat, no phone support.

twist.text: Bad free-tier experiences create negative word-of-mouth. Ignoring free users can damage the brand overall.

climax.text: Free users need enough support to succeed but not so much that they drain the support team's time.

punchline.text: Free users need help but pay nothing. Support is freemium's hidden cost.

quiz.question: How do companies manage support costs for free users?
options: They provide the same support as paid users
Restrict free tier to community forums and self-service help

details.summary: Free users often generate support requests that cost real money to resolve but produce zero revenue. When millions of free users contact support with questions, report bugs, and request help, the support burden can overwhelm teams designed to serve a much smaller number of paying customers.
details.whyItMatters: Support costs per user often exceed infrastructure costs, making the support burden one of freemium's most underestimated expenses..
takeaways: Free users generate support requests that cost money to resolve
Support costs per user often exceed hosting and infrastructure costs
Self-service documentation and community forums reduce the support burden

faq.question: How do freemium companies manage support costs for free users?
faq.answer: Community forums where users help each other. Extensive self-service documentation and knowledge bases. AI-powered chatbots handling common questions. Limiting human support access to paying customers only. Prioritizing paid customer support while free users wait longer or self-serve.

faq.question: Should free users receive any human support at all?
faq.answer: Many successful freemium companies offer no human support to free users. Slack, Figma, and Notion direct free users to documentation and community forums. This approach is sustainable because users willing to troubleshoot independently self-select as engaged users likely to convert.
